root_cause: Inspect._get_signature computes `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` and then uses it as a string. A class decorated with @functools.lru_cache that has __qualname__ in __slots__ exposes __qualname__ as a member_descriptor, not a str, so later string handling raises.
best_solution: In rich/_inspect.py Inspect._get_signature, keep the existing `name or getattr(obj, '__qualname__', name)` expression (a caller-supplied name still wins), then add a type guard: if qualname is not a str, try getattr(obj, '__name__', name); if that is not a str either, fall back to name. The statement spells this out: 'checking the type of __qualname__ falling back to __name__ and if that isn't a str using the already provided fallback'. The fix works because it only changes behavior when the attribute is not a string, so normal objects render exactly as before.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_inspect.py::test_qualname_in_slots: builds `@lru_cache class Klass: __slots__ = ('__qualname__',)` and asserts inspect(Klass) raises nothing. It checks no output format. The existing PASS_TO_PASS render tests (test_render, test_inspect_coroutine, test_inspect_module_with_class, test_inspect_builtin_function_only_python311, test_can_handle_special_characters_in_docstrings[*]) pin exact output, so the precedence of `name` over `obj.__qualname__` and the empty-name fallback must stay as they were.
locating_signals: The title and body name `inspect` and `__qualname__`. Grepping rich/_inspect.py for __qualname__ finds the one `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` line in _get_signature. The function is not named in the statement, but the grep has only two hits (the other is get_object_types_mro_as_strings, which is harmless because an f-string calls str()).
our_outcome_summary: v4 and v7 passed; v6 and v8 failed. v4 and v7 both kept `name or getattr(...)` and added the gold isinstance/__name__ fallback, plus a harmless str() tweak in get_object_types_mro_as_strings. v7 also left a stray reproduce_issue.py, which was harmless. v6 replaced the `or` with `qualname = name; if not isinstance(qualname, str): ...`. Since name is usually '' (a str), the __qualname__ fallback never ran and signatures came out as 'async def ():'. That broke 7 PASS_TO_PASS tests, including test_inspect_coroutine and test_inspect_builtin_function_only_python311. v8 reversed the precedence and always preferred obj.__qualname__ over the caller's name, so attribute rows became 'def Foo.__init__' instead of 'def __init__'. That broke test_render, test_inspect_module_with_class and the special-character docstring tests (7 failed). v8 also used a nested multi-line f-string that only parses on Python 3.12+. Both failures came from rewriting working logic instead of adding a guard next to it.
generalizable_lesson: For a 'handle an unusual value' bugfix, keep the original expression unchanged and add a type guard after it that only acts on the bad case. Do not rewrite the expression into if-chains: `a or b` falls back when a is falsy (e.g. ''), which `if not isinstance(a, str)` does not reproduce, and reordering fallbacks changes precedence. Before finishing, run the module's existing tests (pytest tests/test_<module>.py) as well as the new repro; render/snapshot tests will catch an accidental change in output.
acceptable_alternatives: Any guard that only acts when getattr(obj, '__qualname__') is not a str and keeps `name or ...` precedence, e.g. `if not isinstance(qualname, str): qualname = str(getattr(obj, '__name__', '') or name)`. Also accepting Text instances (as v4 did) is fine.
